black_cumin.season: Cool-season annual. Sow in early spring (or autumn in mild climates); flowers in early summer, seed pods mature by mid-to-late summer.
black_cumin.water: Medium. Water regularly while establishing; established plants tolerate short dry spells. Avoid waterlogged soil.
black_cumin.harvest: Harvest seed pods once they dry and turn brown/black, before they split open, roughly 3-4 months after sowing.
black_cumin.npk: Low nutrient demand. Fertilize only if soil is visibly poor; if needed, a light nitrogen feed is usually enough. Avoid heavy feeding.
black_cumin.source: General horticultural references on Nigella sativa cultivation (e.g. hortiedu.uniag.sk); verify against your local extension guidance before publishing.

sweet_pea.season: Cool-season annual. Sow in early spring (or autumn in mild-winter climates for an earlier bloom); flowers through late spring into summer.
sweet_pea.water: Medium to high, especially once flowering starts. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged; mulch helps retain moisture.
sweet_pea.harvest: Not typically grown for food; harvest as cut flowers by picking blooms regularly (every 2-3 days) to encourage more flowering. Seeds are mildly toxic if eaten - note this in the UI if the audience includes home gardeners.
sweet_pea.npk: Low nitrogen, moderate phosphorus/potassium. Too much nitrogen produces foliage at the expense of flowers. A bloom-booster (higher P-K) feed works well once buds form.
sweet_pea.source: General horticultural references on Lathyrus odoratus cultivation; verify against your local extension guidance before publishing.

onion.season: Cool-season biennial grown as an annual. Plant in early spring (or autumn for overwintering varieties in mild climates).
onion.water: Medium, consistent moisture, about 2.5 cm (1 in) per week. Reduce watering in the final 2-3 weeks before harvest to help bulbs cure.
onion.harvest: Ready in roughly 90-120 days, when the leafy tops yellow and fall over. Cure bulbs in a dry, well-ventilated spot for 1-2 weeks before storage.
onion.npk: Moderate nitrogen early for leaf growth, then shift to phosphorus/potassium as bulbs form. Stop nitrogen once bulbing begins, since excess nitrogen delays maturity.
onion.source: General horticultural references on Allium cepa cultivation; verify against your local extension guidance before publishing.
